articleBody:
- [ ] Width and height measurements — Record the exact finished rough opening dimensions to ensure panel compatibility.
- [ ] Headroom clearance check — Measure the vertical distance between the top of the door opening and the ceiling joists to confirm track clearance.
- [ ] Sideroom measurement — Verify at least 3.75 to 5 inches of clearance on each jamb for vertical track brackets.
- [ ] Backroom depth verification — Ensure ceiling space extends inward further than the door height plus opener rail requirements.
- [ ] Jamb wood condition test — Press an awl into wood jambs and the header to confirm framing is completely free of moisture rot.
- [ ] Wind-load rating verification — Check that replacement door specifications meet local wind-pressure requirements and feature permanent manufacturer labeling.
- [ ] Opener horsepower match — Confirm your existing or planned opener has sufficient horsepower and safety sensors to manage the door's total weight.
- [ ] Dedicated electrical outlet check — Verify an unswitched ceiling electrical outlet is present and operational for the opener motor.

How to Use This Checklist:
Run through each check before ordering materials or tearing out existing overhead panels. Catching framing decay or insufficient ceiling headroom early prevents mid-project delays and ensures your replacement door operates quietly and seals tightly against Colorado drafts.
